candidates.title: Quantization as Survival Analysis: Discrete-Time Proportional Hazards Models for Bit-Width Collapse Prediction
candidates.abstract: Post-training quantization of large language models (LLMs) requires careful allocation of bit-widths across heterogeneous architectural components. Existing sensitivity metrics rely on gradient norms, Hessian traces, or activation ranges, all of which are computed at a fixed bit-width and do not account for the sequential, multi-stage nature of progressive compression. We propose to reframe quantization fragility as a survival problem: each transformer block is treated as a unit subject to a failure event—a critical performance collapse—as bit-width decreases from 16 to 2 bits through an ordered schedule <inline-formula> <tex-math notation="LaTeX">$\mathcal {B} = \langle 16,12,8,6,5,4,3,2 \rangle $ </tex-math></inline-formula>. We build a discrete-time interval-censored survival dataset from one-at-a-time block quantization experiments and fit a discrete-time proportional hazards model via complementary log-log (cloglog) regression. The resulting hazard ratios provide statistically grounded, architecture- aware predictors of collapse timing. We demonstrate that depth-normalised position (HR = 8.54, <inline-formula> <tex-math notation="LaTeX">$p \lt 10^{-4}$ </tex-math></inline-formula>) and weight variance-to-mean ratio (HR = 3.98, <inline-formula> <tex-math notation="LaTeX">$p \lt 10^{-3}$ </tex-math></inline-formula>) are the dominant structural predictors of quantization vulnerability, while attention head density provides a protective effect (HR = 0.40, <inline-formula> <tex-math notation="LaTeX">$p \lt 0.002$ </tex-math></inline-formula>). A survival-driven mixed-precision allocation (SurvAlloc) derived from these hazard ratios outperforms uniform INT4 quantization by + 1.2–+ 2.7 MMLU points at a comparable memory footprint across TinyLlama-1.1B, Llama-2-7B, OPT-6.7B, and Mistral-7B. The concordance index reaches <inline-formula> <tex-math notation="LaTeX">$0.81~[{0.76, 0.86}]$ </tex-math></inline-formula>, confirmed non-random by a Monte Carlo permutation test (<inline-formula> <tex-math notation="LaTeX">$p \lt 10^{-4}$ </tex-math></inline-formula>).
candidates.reason: IEEE Access論文のDOAJ収録・出版社提供書誌abstractを確認。Transformerの各blockを16→12→8→6→5→4→3→2 bitの順に圧縮した際、性能が大きく崩れる時点を「故障イベント」とみなし、区間打切り離散時間生存データに対する相補対数対数回帰で脆弱性を予測する。推定ハザード比を使うSurvAllocは、TinyLlama-1.1B、Llama-2-7B、OPT-6.7B、Mistral-7Bで、同程度のメモリ使用量の一律INT4に対しMMLUを1.2〜2.7ポイント改善と要旨で報告。LLM推論用の混合精度量子化配分・メモリ圧縮へ直接寄与するためaccept。推論速度の改善は要旨で確認しておらず、本文・詳細条件は未読。
